challenges.title: Birth Year
challenges.task: Print BASIC WAS BORN IN on one line and the year 1964 on the next. Don't type 1964 directly: let the computer calculate 1900 + 64.

requirements.message: Let the computer add 1900 + 64.

hints: The first line is a PRINT with text in quotes.
PRINT can calculate: PRINT 1900 + 64
Don't forget END.

challenges.title: Rectangle
challenges.task: A rectangle is 7 long and 3 wide. Store both in variables with LET, then print AREA = and PERIMETER = on two lines.

requirements.message: Store the length 7 with LET.
Store the width 3 with LET.

hints: LET L = 7 and LET W = 3
Area is L * W, perimeter is 2 * (L + W)
PRINT "AREA = "; L * W

challenges.title: Minutes in a Week
challenges.task: Print how many minutes a week has. Let BASIC multiply days, hours and minutes.

requirements.message: Let the computer multiply days, hours and minutes, like 7 * 24 * 60.

hints: A week has 7 days, a day has 24 hours, an hour has 60 minutes.
PRINT 7 * 24 * 60

challenges.title: The Bigger One
challenges.task: Store 17 in A and 42 in B. Use IF…THEN to print BIGGER = followed by whichever number is bigger.

requirements.message: Use IF … THEN to decide which one is bigger.

hints: IF A > B THEN jump to a line that prints A
Otherwise print B, then jump past the other PRINT
Use STOP or GOTO so only one PRINT runs.

challenges.title: Count by Twos
challenges.task: Print 2, 4, 6 … up to 20, one per line, using a counter and IF…THEN. At most 6 lines.

requirements.message: Repeat with IF … THEN, not with ten PRINT lines.

hints: Start at LET C = 2
PRINT C, then LET C = C + 2
Jump back while C <= 20

challenges.title: Odd Numbers
challenges.task: Print all odd numbers from 1 to 19, one per line, with a FOR loop. At most 4 lines.

requirements.message: Use STEP 2 to skip the even numbers.

hints: FOR I = 1 TO 19 STEP 2
PRINT I, then NEXT I

challenges.title: Little Gauss
challenges.task: Legend says young Carl Friedrich Gauss added the numbers 1 to 100 in seconds. Your program can too: print the sum. At most 6 lines.

requirements.message: Use a FOR loop from 1 to 100.

hints: Start with LET S = 0
FOR I = 1 TO 100, LET S = S + I, NEXT I
Print S after the loop.

challenges.title: Powers of Two
challenges.task: Print the powers of two from 1 to 1024 (1, 2, 4, 8 …), one per line. At most 5 lines.

requirements.message: Use a FOR loop.

hints: FOR I = 0 TO 10, PRINT 2 ^ I, NEXT I

challenges.title: Countdown by Fives
challenges.task: Count down from 50 to 0 in steps of five, one number per line. At most 4 lines.

requirements.message: Count down with STEP -5.

hints: FOR I = 50 TO 0 STEP -5

challenges.title: Square of Stars
challenges.task: Print a square of stars, 4 rows with 4 stars each, using two nested FOR loops.

requirements.message: Use two FOR loops, one inside the other.

hints: The inner loop prints PRINT "*"; four times
An empty PRINT ends each row

challenges.title: Shopping Bag
challenges.task: Three items cost 2.5, 4 and 1.75. Put them in a DATA line, read them, and print TOTAL = with their sum.

requirements.message: Store the prices in a DATA line.
Get the prices with READ.

hints: READ A, B, C reads all three at once
PRINT "TOTAL = "; A + B + C

challenges.title: Weekly Temperature
challenges.task: The temperatures this week were 12, 15, 11, 9, 14, 16 and 14 degrees. Read them in a FOR loop and print AVERAGE = with the average.

requirements.message: Read the temperatures inside a FOR loop.

hints: Add every value to a total T
Seven days: FOR I = 1 TO 7
The average is T / 7

challenges.title: Who Passed?
challenges.task: Eight students scored 45, 67, 89, 32, 50, 71, 49 and 90. A score of 50 or more passes. Print PASSED = with the number of students who passed.

requirements.message: Read the scores in a FOR loop.

hints: Start a counter at 0
IF X < 50 THEN skip the counting line
LET C = C + 1 for every pass

challenges.title: Backwards
challenges.task: Read the six numbers 3, 8, 1, 9, 4 and 7 into a list. Print them in reverse order, one per line.

requirements.message: Read the numbers into a list, like READ A(I).
Print backwards with a negative STEP.

hints: FOR I = 1 TO 6, READ A(I), NEXT I
FOR I = 6 TO 1 STEP -1, PRINT A(I), NEXT I

challenges.title: Double Everything
challenges.task: Read 4, 9, 2, 11 and 6 into a list. Then double every element inside the list in a second loop, and print the list, one per line.

requirements.message: Read the numbers into a list.
Double the elements inside the list, like LET A(I) = A(I) * 2.

hints: First loop: READ A(I)
Second loop: LET A(I) = A(I) * 2
Third loop (or the same one): PRINT A(I)

challenges.title: Lowest and Where
challenges.task: Read 34, 21, 58, 13, 40 and 27 into a list. Print LOWEST = with the smallest value, and POSITION = with its place in the list.

requirements.message: Read the numbers into a list.

hints: Remember the position M of the smallest so far, starting with M = 1
IF A(I) >= A(M) THEN skip, otherwise LET M = I
A(M) is the value, M is the position

challenges.title: Round to Cents
challenges.task: The prices 2.344, 7.891 and 5.678 have too many decimals. Read them and print each one rounded to two decimals, one per line.

requirements.message: Round with INT, like INT(P * 100 + 0.5) / 100.

hints: Multiply by 100, add 0.5, cut with INT, divide by 100
Read the three prices in a FOR loop

challenges.title: The Long Side
challenges.task: A right triangle has the short sides 5 and 12. Print the length of the long side, using SQR.

requirements.message: Use SQR for the square root.

hints: Pythagoras: the long side is SQR(A * A + B * B)

challenges.title: Divisors of 36
challenges.task: Print every number that divides 36 evenly, from 1 to 36, one per line. Check each number with INT.

requirements.message: Check with INT: D divides N when N / D = INT(N / D).

hints: FOR D = 1 TO 36
Skip the PRINT when 36 / D <> INT(36 / D)

challenges.title: Digit Sum
challenges.task: Add up the digits of 4096 (4 + 0 + 9 + 6) and print the result. Don't type the digits: take the number apart with INT in a loop.

requirements.message: Start from the number 4096.
Take the number apart with INT.

hints: The last digit of N is N - 10 * INT(N / 10)
Then remove it: LET N = INT(N / 10)
Repeat while N > 0

challenges.title: Banner
challenges.task: Print a banner: a line of 8 stars, WELCOME, the star line again, TO BASIC, and the star line a third time. Write the star line only once, in a subroutine.

requirements.message: Print the star line with a subroutine.
End the subroutine with RETURN.

hints: 1000 PRINT "********" and 1010 RETURN
Call GOSUB 1000 three times
STOP before the subroutine

challenges.title: Squares by Subroutine
challenges.task: Write a subroutine that prints the square of X. Call it three times, with X = 3, 7 and 12.

requirements.message: Call the subroutine three times.
End the subroutine with RETURN.

hints: LET X = 3, GOSUB 1000, LET X = 7, GOSUB 1000 …
The subroutine: PRINT X * X, RETURN

challenges.title: Stars on Request
challenges.task: Write a subroutine that prints a row of N stars. Use it to print rows with 1, 3 and 5 stars.

requirements.message: Print the rows with a subroutine.
Use a FOR loop inside the subroutine.

hints: Main program: LET N = 1, GOSUB 1000, and so on
Subroutine: FOR I = 1 TO N, PRINT "*";, NEXT I, PRINT, RETURN

challenges.title: Cube Function
challenges.task: Define a function FNC that cubes a number. Use it to print the cubes of 1 to 5, one per line.

requirements.message: Define the function with DEF FN.

hints: DEF FNC(X) = X * X * X
FOR I = 1 TO 5, PRINT FNC(I), NEXT I

challenges.title: Kilometers to Miles
challenges.task: One kilometer is 0.621371 miles. Define a function that converts kilometers to miles, rounded to one decimal. Print a table from 10 to 50 km in steps of 10, with km in the first column and miles in the second.

requirements.message: Put the conversion into a DEF function.
Count from 10 to 50 with STEP 10.

hints: Round to one decimal: INT(X * 10 + 0.5) / 10
PRINT K, FNM(K)

challenges.title: What Divides 84?
challenges.task: Define a remainder function FNR(D) = N - D * INT(N / D). Set N = 84 and print every number from 1 to 10 that divides 84 evenly.

requirements.message: Use a DEF function for the remainder.

hints: DEF FNR(D) = N - D * INT(N / D)
FOR D = 1 TO 10
IF FNR(D) <> 0 THEN skip the PRINT

challenges.title: Fix the Sum
challenges.task: This program should print SUM = 15 (the numbers 1 to 5 added up), but it has two bugs. Run it, read the error, and fix it.
challenges.starter:
10 REM ADD 1 TO 5
20 LET S = 0
30 FOR I = 1 TO 5
40 LET S = I
50 NEXT J
60 PRINT "SUM = "; S
70 END

requirements.message: The sum must grow: LET S = S + I.

hints: NEXT must name the same variable as its FOR.
Line 40 overwrites S instead of adding to it.

challenges.title: Fix the Table
challenges.task: This program should print a table of cubes for 1 to 4, with the header N and CUBE printed once, and values in two columns. Find and fix the bugs.
challenges.starter:
10 REM TABLE OF CUBES
20 FOR N = 1 TO 4
30 PRINT "N", "CUBE"
40 PRINT N; N * N
50 NEXT N
60 END

requirements.message: A cube is N * N * N.

hints: The header is printed in every round. Move it before the loop, for example to line 15.
Line 40 calculates the square, not the cube.
A comma puts the cube in its own column.

challenges.title: Hollow Square
challenges.task: Print a hollow square, 5 stars wide and 5 rows high: full rows at the top and bottom, and in between only the first and last star, with spaces inside. Spaces count.

requirements.message: Use nested FOR loops for rows and columns.

hints: Loop over rows R and columns C, both 1 to 5
Print a star if R or C is 1 or 5, otherwise a space
Use IF lines that jump to the star PRINT

challenges.title: Number Triangle
challenges.task: Print a triangle of numbers: the first row is 1, the second 1 2, the third 1 2 3, up to the fifth row 1 2 3 4 5.

requirements.message: Use two nested FOR loops.

hints: The inner loop runs from 1 to the row number R
PRINT C; keeps the numbers on one line
An empty PRINT ends each row

challenges.title: Staircase
challenges.task: Print a staircase of # signs that leans to the right: 4 rows, the first with 3 spaces and 1 #, the last with no spaces and 4 #. Spaces count.

requirements.message: Use nested FOR loops.

hints: Row R has 4 - R spaces and R signs
Spaces first: PRINT " ";, then PRINT "#";

challenges.title: How Many Sevens?
challenges.task: Count how often 7 appears in 7, 3, 7, 1, 7, 9, 2, 7 and print SEVENS = with the count.

requirements.message: Read the numbers from a DATA line.

hints: Read each number in a FOR loop
IF X <> 7 THEN skip the counting line

challenges.title: Second Place
challenges.task: Read 14, 52, 33, 47, 8 and 29 into a list and print the second biggest value. Any method works, for example sorting first.

requirements.message: Read the numbers into a list.

hints: Easiest way: sort the list from biggest to smallest, then print A(2)
Bubble sort with IF A(I) >= A(I + 1) for descending order

challenges.title: Highest First
challenges.task: Sort 5, 12, 3, 9 and 1 from highest to lowest and print them, one per line.

requirements.message: Keep the DATA in the original order: 5, 12, 3, 9, 1.
Swap with a helper variable, like LET T = A(I).

hints: Bubble sort with two FOR loops
For highest first: skip the swap when A(I) >= A(I + 1)

challenges.title: Three Coins
challenges.task: Toss three coins, where 1 means heads and 0 means tails. Try all combinations with nested loops and print WAYS = with how many give exactly two heads.

requirements.message: Use three nested FOR loops, one per coin.

hints: FOR A = 0 TO 1, FOR B = 0 TO 1, FOR C = 0 TO 1
Two heads means A + B + C = 2

challenges.title: Eight or More
challenges.task: How often do two dice add up to 8 or more? Try all 36 combinations and print WAYS = with the count, and PERCENT = with the chance in percent, rounded to a whole number.

requirements.message: Try all combinations with two nested FOR loops.

hints: Count the combinations where A + B >= 8
The chance in percent is W / 36 * 100
Round with INT(X + 0.5)

challenges.title: Age in Days
challenges.task: Ask for an age in years with INPUT and print DAYS = with roughly how many days that is (365 per year).

requirements.message: Ask for the age with INPUT.

hints: INPUT A
PRINT "DAYS = "; A * 365

challenges.title: Bigger of Two
challenges.task: Ask for two numbers with INPUT and print BIGGER = with the bigger one.

requirements.message: Ask for the numbers with INPUT.

hints: INPUT A, B asks for both
IF A > B THEN jump to the line that prints A

challenges.title: Times Table on Demand
challenges.task: Ask for a number N with INPUT, then print its times table from 1 to 10: the multiplier in the first column, the result in the second.

requirements.message: Ask for the number with INPUT.
Use a FOR loop for the table.

hints: INPUT N
FOR I = 1 TO 10, PRINT I, N * I, NEXT I

challenges.title: Running Average
challenges.task: Keep asking for numbers with INPUT until the user types 0. Then print AVERAGE = with the average of the numbers before the 0.

requirements.message: Stop when the number is 0, like IF X = 0 THEN …

hints: Keep a total T and a count C
Check for 0 before adding
The average is T / C

challenges.title: Password Check
challenges.task: Ask for a password with INPUT P$. If it isn't BASIC, print WRONG and ask again. When it's right, print WELCOME.

requirements.message: Read the password into a text variable, like INPUT P$.
Compare it with IF P$ = "BASIC" THEN …

hints: INPUT P$
IF P$ = "BASIC" THEN jump to the WELCOME line
Otherwise PRINT "WRONG" and GOTO back to the INPUT

challenges.title: Greeting Machine
challenges.task: Store the names ADA, ALAN and GRACE in a DATA line. Read them one by one and print HELLO, followed by the name, for each.

requirements.message: Read the names into a text variable, like READ N$.

hints: DATA "ADA", "ALAN", "GRACE"
FOR I = 1 TO 3, READ N$, PRINT "HELLO, "; N$, NEXT I
challenges.expectedOutput:
HELLO, ADA
HELLO, ALAN
HELLO, GRACE

challenges.title: Adding Lists
challenges.task: Two shops sold 3, 5, 2 and 8 items, and 4, 1, 6 and 2 items over four days. Use MAT READ to read both lists, MAT to add them, and MAT PRINT to print the daily totals.

requirements.message: Read the lists with MAT READ.
Add the lists with MAT C = A + B.
Print the result with MAT PRINT.

hints: MAT READ A, B reads both lists from one DATA line
MAT C = A + B, then MAT PRINT C
